Predict from a brms-passthrough flexybayes fit

Source: R/emit_brms.R
predict.flexybayes_brms.Rd

Delegates to brms's posterior_epred() (response-scale posterior mean) or posterior_linpred() (linear-predictor scale) on the live brmsfit carried at $brms. The parent predict.flexybayes() path uses a $glm$linear.predictors point estimate that handles only the original-data case. This subclass override accepts newdata and returns the posterior-mean prediction (per-row mean over draws), or the full posterior matrix when summary = FALSE.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'flexybayes_brms'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("response", "link"),
  re_formula = NULL,
  se.fit = FALSE,
  summary = TRUE,
  classify = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  allow_new_levels = FALSE,
  mean_by = NULL,
  n_draws = 1000L,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A flexybayes_brms object.

newdata

Optional data.frame at which to predict. When omitted, returns the in-sample posterior summary. On a model with an offset() brms evaluates the offset on newdata, so newdata needs every column the offset reads. An absent one refuses with newdata_offset_missing instead of being taken as zero.

type

"response" (default. posterior_epred) or "link" (posterior_linpred).

re_formula

Forwarded to brms; NULL (default) includes all random effects, NA excludes them (population-level).

se.fit

Logical: if TRUE, returns a list with fit (posterior mean) and se.fit (posterior SD).

summary

Logical: if TRUE (default), summarise across draws to a numeric vector. If FALSE, return the draws x rows posterior matrix.

classify

The factors to break a predicted-value table down by: a character value ("Variety", "Variety:env") or a one-sided formula (~ Variety). The factors may be fixed or random, and the table follows ASReml's default rules, described under predict.flexybayes_inla(). On this engine the values come from the posterior draws. A level combination the data never held is drawn from its fitted normal distribution. NULL (the default) is the historical behaviour.

level

Credible level for the classify table's interval, or for the predictive interval with allow_new_levels = TRUE, as a proportion. Default 0.95.

allow_new_levels

Logical. TRUE returns the posterior predictive of the rows of newdata, observation noise included, in which a level the fit did not see is drawn from its fitted standard deviation: brms::posterior_predict(allow_new_levels = TRUE, sample_new_levels = "gaussian"). The table matches the INLA method's. See predict.flexybayes_inla() for the structures it is built for and the refusals. Its estimate, sd, lower and upper are the mean, standard deviation and quantiles of the draws. FALSE (the default) leaves the paths above unchanged.

mean_by

With allow_new_levels = TRUE, the columns of newdata whose combinations define the sets of rows to average, as a character vector or a one-sided formula (~ TRIAL). NULL predicts each row.

n_draws

With allow_new_levels = TRUE, the number of posterior draws used, at most the number the fit holds. Default 1000.

...

Forwarded to brms::posterior_epred() / brms::posterior_linpred().

Value

One of five shapes, by argument. With classify set, the marginal-means table for those factors. With allow_new_levels = TRUE, the fb_predict_new table described in predict.flexybayes_inla(). Otherwise with summary = FALSE, the draws x rows posterior matrix. With se.fit = TRUE, a list of fit (posterior mean per row) and se.fit (posterior SD per row). And by default a numeric vector of posterior means, one per row of newdata or of the fitted data.

Details

Population-level vs. group-level prediction follows brms's re_formula convention: the default re_formula = NULL includes all random effects. Pass re_formula = NA for population-level predictions only.
